s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological condition with worsening symptoms over time, primarily affecting one side of the body, with comorbid mental health symptoms
salient_findings: Difficulty on the left side of the body
key_facts: Initial symptoms started in 2013
Symptoms worsened in 2020
Patient attended physiotherapy
Physiotherapy was initially daily, then reduced to 2-3 sessions per week
Patient has comorbid depression and anxiety
Main difficulties are on the left side of the body
Initial brain MRI showed brain aging and partially empty sella turcica
Follow-up brain MRI showed mild cerebral atrophy and micro-ischemic focal lesions
Initial MMSE score was 24/30
Follow-up MMSE score was 27/30

shortlist.label: Stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Focal lesions in periventricular and deep white matter, worsening symptoms over time

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological condition with worsening symptoms, primarily affecting one side of the body

shortlist.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological condition with asymmetric symptoms, comorbid mental health symptoms

shortlist.label: Primary Lateral Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological condition with worsening symptoms, primarily affecting motor function

shortlist.label: Binswanger's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Micro-ischemic focal lesions, progressive neurological condition with cognitive decline

raw.rationale: The presence of micro-ischemic focal lesions in the periventricular and deep white matter of the cerebral hemispheres on the follow-up brain MRI, along with the worsening of symptoms over time, supports the diagnosis of a vascular condition such as stroke.

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis
rejected.why: The lack of specific findings on physical examination and the absence of lesions typical for MS in the brain MRI make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more pronounced cognitive decline and specific motor symptoms, which are not detailed in the case report.

rejected.label: Primary Lateral Sclerosis
rejected.why: The presence of micro-ischemic lesions and the pattern of symptom progression do not align with the typical presentation of PLS, which primarily affects the upper motor neurons.

rejected.label: Binswanger's Disease
rejected.why: While the patient's age and the presence of white matter lesions could suggest Binswanger's, the clinical presentation and the specific pattern of lesions do not fully align with this diagnosis.
